bull.b: Zelsuvmi is showing meaningful commercial adoption after launch, with strong year-over-year revenue growth and substantial cumulative sales. Continued patient treatment and prescription expansion can strengthen Pelthos’s revenue base, improve operating leverage, and support broader investment in its dermatology portfolio.

Broader formulary access reduces a key barrier to prescriptions and expands the addressable patient pool for Zelsuvmi. Coverage across commercial and Medicaid lives gives the product a stronger platform for durable utilization growth as prescribers and patients become more familiar with it.

The proposed Castle Creek transaction could diversify Pelthos beyond its marketed infectious-disease franchise by adding a late-stage dermatology asset and a cell and gene therapy platform. This may broaden future growth opportunities and leverage Pelthos’s existing dermatology commercial capabilities.

bear.b: Pelthos’s revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable profitability, as large net and operating losses remain far ahead of the current revenue base. This weak earnings profile can constrain reinvestment, increase dependence on financing, and make execution of future launches more financially demanding.

Negative equity combined with rising debt materially reduces the company’s balance-sheet cushion. This leaves Pelthos more exposed to financing and dilution risk, while limiting flexibility to absorb operating setbacks or fund product development without additional external capital.

A higher gross-to-net rate means a larger portion of nominal product sales may be absorbed by discounts, rebates, or access costs before revenue is recognized. If this level persists, it can limit net revenue conversion and make margin improvement harder even as prescription demand expands.
